div.div:
1. The Law: NetworkPolicy (K8s Object)
This is the high-level "intent" you write in YAML. It’s just a set of rules saying "Pod A can talk to Pod B." By itself, this YAML file does nothing—it’s just a record in the Kubernetes database.

div.div:
2. The Translator: Calico
Calico is the Controller. It sits on every node in your cluster and watches the Kubernetes API. When it sees you’ve created a NetworkPolicy, it thinks: "Okay, I need to make sure this node actually blocks or allows this traffic." Calico’s job is to take that human-readable YAML and translate it into a language the Linux Kernel understands.

div.div: When a packet arrives at the FORWARD hook, , the Linux Kernel pause and looks at the iptables rules Calico wrote and decides to either ACCEPT or DROP the packet based on your original policy.
